attack_plan.narrative: On a fateful day in March 2015, an Airbus A320 operated by Germanwings, flight number 4U9525, crashed in the French Alps near Digne, resulting in the loss of all 150 passengers and crew members. Eyewitnesses reported a struggle in the cockpit, suggesting that the pilot had attempted to force entry from the outside. The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, was at the controls at the time of the incident. According to a former colleague, Lubitz had faced significant personal challenges, including burnout and depression, which may have contributed to his actions. While the official investigation continues, it is believed that these personal struggles could have played a role in the tragic outcome. The aircraft, one of the older models in the fleet, was delivered in November 1990, potentially adding stress to the already difficult conditions for the crew.
